sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was not smooth: FY2021 revenue jumped 89.1% to $16.1 billion, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12.2 billion [F6][F7][D241][D292].
REGEN-COV U.S. sales of $5.83 billion contributed 66.4pp of FY2021's growth [S48][D582].
The FY2022 reversal followed REGEN-COV sales to zero, a 36.3pp drag, as new SARS-CoV-2 variants were not susceptible to the treatment [S49][D585][P7].
Since then growth has slowed to 5.6% a year over FY2022..FY2025, with FY2025 up only 1.0% [D767][D440].
The mix has inverted: net product sales fell to 44.0% of revenue in FY2025 from 75.4% in FY2021, while collaboration revenue reached 51.1% [D505][D493][D521].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% to $5.24 billion in FY2025, adding 9.3pp of growth, on higher Dupixent sales [S52][D591][D592][P9].
U.S. EYLEA sales fell 42.4% to $2.75 billion, a 14.2pp drag, on competitive pressure, compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition [S43][D577][D578][P10].
EYLEA HD partly offset that, rising 36.3% to $1.64 billion and adding 3.1pp, on higher volumes [S64][D613][D614][P11].
Operating income fell 10.3% in FY2025 against 1.0% revenue growth, so there was no operating leverage [F20][D441][D440].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 is the window low, against a 34.6% median and a 55.7% FY2021 high [F30][D749][D751][D750].
It has fallen four straight years, from 55.7% in FY2021, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].
In FY2025 R&D took 4.7pp of margin as it rose 14.0% to $5.85 billion, while SG&A added 2.0pp as it fell 8.6% [D465][X34][D455][D466][D456].
The SG&A decline was primarily lower charitable contributions to the Good Days patient assistance fund [P5].
Net margin held at 31.4%, 6.5pp above operating margin, helped by other income of $1.65 billion and a 13.9% tax rate [F50][D797][X117][D427].
Operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income, in line with the 1.10x window median [F80][F40][D428][D787].
Free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x net income and a 28.4% margin, above the 26.4% median [F100][F40][D429][D425][D757].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898 million, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [F90][D447][D424][D430].
Stock-based compensation of $994 million absorbed 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash reached $16.9 billion, 117.7% of revenue, the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a -50.7% median [D434][D435][D780][D781].
Debt is a flat $1.99 billion and the current ratio is 4.13x, above the 3.97x median [F187][F180][D766].
Buybacks of $3.44 billion plus a first dividend of $370 million used 93.3% of free cash flow [X137][X140][D437].
Diluted shares fell 5.6%, so diluted EPS grew 8.2% against 2.1% net income growth [D459][D444][D442].
The four-year, 30.7pp operating-margin slide is the main concern, driven by R&D intensity and EYLEA erosion [R1][F26][F30].
R&D at 40.8% of revenue is the 100th percentile of eight peers against a 20.1% median, so margin recovery depends on that spend paying off [D420][D778][D779].

Data quality: FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table is a later recast ($5.15 billion and $6.56 billion) versus $6.71 billion and $7.86 billion first reported, so growth spanning those years mixes presentations [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
Return on average equity fell to 14.9%, the 25th percentile of eight peers against a 38.7% median [D439][D784][D785].
Whether operating margin holds at the 24.9% FY2025 low or falls further, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D749].
Whether U.S. EYLEA sales stabilize above $2.75 billion or keep declining toward the EYLEA HD offset [S43][S64].
Whether R&D as a share of revenue falls back toward the 34.6% median from 40.8% [D420][D760].
